### Swipe actions
Reveals a list row's actions when a person swipes it sideways, or presses its actions button.

Component ID: `swipe-actions`

[Component documentation](https://www.expressivecss.com/swipe-actions.html.md) · [Repository source](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/blob/master/docs/src/pages/swipe-actions.astro) · [Matching tag](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/tree/v0.15.0)

Contract: ExpressiveCSS 0.15.0

Contract SHA-256: `feefdae952b13cabd2c21e9f89d6e99902118c5c219ef116733961ee60d46fa0`

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `auto-init`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Example: An inbox where each message can be archived or deleted takes swipe actions with an actions button per row; a row with one obvious action shows that button in the row instead.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Upstream: web-extension-inventory-reviewed (2026-10-24); [evidence](https://m3.material.io/components).

Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. The inventory page renders client-side, so this review relies on the 2026-09-13 inventory review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.

Support (2026-10-24, `llm.md#swipe-actions`): A touch swipe toward a row's inline start that reveals its .swipe-actions group, opening past half the group's width or on a flick and closing short of it, a [data-swipe-toggle] button with aria-expanded, focus on an action opening its row, Escape, an outside tap or an action closing it, one open row per list, an expressive:swipetoggle event and onToggle callback with { row, open }, open(row) and close(), right-to-left pages and reduced motion.

Web adaptation: Touch events with a non-passive touchmove, because a pointer drag the browser takes for a pan ends in pointercancel. The row slides by a translate on one custom property, and the actions wait past its inline end in a list clipped on the inline axis, so focus on a closed row's action scrolls nothing. The author names the toggle and the actions; the script keeps aria-expanded.

Known boundary: Swipe reveal, the slide limit, short, vertical, mouse, two-finger and cancelled drags, the toggle, focus on an action, Escape, an outside tap, closing after an action, one open row, the event and onToggle, right-to-left pages, reduced motion and destroy() are checked in a browser, with real touch in Chromium and dispatched touch events in Firefox and WebKit; real phones, flick velocity, pen input, spoken output and forced colors remain unverified. Actions only on the inline-end side, and no full swipe that runs an action.

Full parity remains unassessed. [Capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#swipe-actions).

#### Contract

Add `swipeable` to a `.list`. A row with actions holds a `<button data-swipe-toggle>` as its trailing action, then a `.swipe-actions` group of buttons as its last child. `AutoInit()` starts every `.list.swipeable`.

A touch swipe toward the row's inline start, which is left in a left-to-right page, slides the row with the finger and brings the actions in from the other edge. Released past half the actions' width, or with a flick, the row stays open; released short of that, it slides back. A swipe only reveals the actions, and none of them runs until a person presses it. A swipe the other way closes an open row. A drag that moves up or down first scrolls as usual, a second finger or a cancelled touch puts the row back, and a mouse drag never swipes.

The toggle opens and closes the row for keyboard, mouse and switch users, and the script keeps its `aria-expanded` in step. The actions stay in the tab order and the accessibility tree while the row is closed, and focus on one opens its row. One row in a list is open at a time. A tap or focus outside the open row closes it, and so does Escape inside it. Escape on an action, or pressing one, closes the row and moves focus from the action to the toggle. The page handles what each action does.

#### Syntax

```html
<ul class="list swipeable" aria-label="Inbox">
  <li>
    <span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">mail</span>
    Weekly report
    <button type="button" class="icon-button" data-swipe-toggle aria-label="Actions for Weekly report">
      <span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">more_horiz</span>
    </button>
    <span class="swipe-actions">
      <button type="button" class="icon-button" aria-label="Archive Weekly report">
        <span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">archive</span>
      </button>
      <button type="button" class="icon-button" aria-label="Delete Weekly report">
        <span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">delete</span>
      </button>
    </span>
  </li>
</ul>
```

#### Options

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onToggle` | Function | `null` | Called when a row opens or closes, with `{ row, open }`. |

#### Methods

- `.open(row)`: Opens a row of the list, closing the one that was open.
- `.close()`: Closes the open row, if there is one.
- `.destroy()`: Removes the listeners, closes the open row without an event and removes the toggles' `aria-expanded`.

#### Also documented

The Swipe actions section of the [API reference](https://www.expressivecss.com/llm.md) also covers Tokens.

#### Rules

- `swipeable-rows-open-without-swiping`: Give each .swipeable row with .swipe-actions a [data-swipe-toggle] button. Swiping is a path-based gesture; the toggle is the single-pointer alternative WCAG 2.5.1 requires, and focus on an action opens the row for keyboard users.
